lede: The biggest thing on the board this week is Carhenge — on Tuesday, September 30, both HARC and a special Town Council session take up the proposed redevelopment at 700 W. Pacific Avenue, with HARC reviewing the building designs and the Council hearing an appeal of the lot subdivision that a law firm filed after P&Z approved it in July. San Miguel County commissioners are also taking a first hard look at a proposed Employee Housing Impact Fee. Elsewhere, budget season is in full swing across the region, Original Thinkers kicks off Thursday, and the Annual San Miguel River Cleanup is Saturday.

notable.stake: HARC reviews all three building clusters of the Carhenge redevelopment in one session.
Council hears appeal of the Carhenge lot consolidation — outcome could stall or advance the project.
Commissioners discuss a new Employee Housing Impact Fee that could affect county development costs.
Final architecture review for 15 employee apartments and 4 new multifamily units in Mountain Village.
